clips.send: Someone grinding 60-hour weeks at a new business sends this to a friend ready to quit, proof that every plane needs full throttle before it ever reaches cruising altitude.
clips.caption:
Kevin Trudeau says making money works exactly like flying a plane.

A pilot doesn't ease onto the runway. He holds the brake, pushes the throttle to full, and only then lets go - and the plane sits there building power before it ever moves.

It takes everything, full throttle, the whole climb, just to get off the ground and up to cruising altitude.

Only then does the pilot pull back the throttle and flip on autopilot.

That's the part everyone skips: wanting the autopilot stage while they're still sitting at the end of the runway.

Are you still building power, or are you trying to cruise before you've even taken off?

clips.send: A new business owner working for free right now sends this to a friend ready to quit, proof that the founders of a $2 billion app and a $9.5 billion restaurant chain both worked unpaid and exhausted before any of it paid off.
clips.caption:
Kevin Trudeau points to two founders most people romanticize but never actually copy.

One built a $2 billion a year super app. Before that: 18 to 20 hour days, seven days a week, unpaid, working out of a one-room office in Malaysia with no air conditioning and no Wi-Fi.

The other, Todd Graves, is now worth $9.5 billion. To raise money for his first restaurant, he worked 90-hour weeks in an oil refinery, then fished for salmon in Alaska.

Neither of them started comfortable. Both of them refused to stay that way.

What are you willing to do before it pays off?

clips.send: A small business owner who can't afford a $100,000 copywriter sends this to a friend starting an online store, proof that an AI system can now get close to that same result for free.
clips.caption:
Kevin Trudeau says one of his students built something that should scare every $100,000-a-project copywriter.

The guy learned copywriting from Kevin and others, then built an AI system that writes sales copy from nothing more than a few answered questions.

He ran it head to head against real, paid, professional copywriters in A/B tests. Kevin's words: it did as good, and in some cases better.

Kevin charges people $100,000 plus a cut of sales to write copy personally. This system gets close to that same result for free.

Would you still pay six figures for copy if a few typed answers got you most of the way there?

#kevintrudeau #copywriting #aitools #onlinebusiness #marketingtips #makemoneyonline

clips.send: A homeowner whose house has sat unsold for months sends this to a friend about to relist with the same realtor, proof that photos, staging and asking about the buyer - not reciting room names - is what actually sells a house.
clips.caption:
Kevin Trudeau tells the story of a house that sat on the market for six months with one realtor, then sold in one week with another: Josh Altman.

Same house. Same buyers out there. What changed was everything the first realtor skipped.

Altman takes different photos, stages the house properly, and writes the listing differently. Then, walking a buyer through, instead of "this is the living room, this is the kitchen," he asks where they're from, what they do, what's bringing them to the area.

He's building a connection. The other realtor is reciting a floor plan.

Which one would make you want to buy?
